The m/z-direct Mummichog method independently recovers galactose metabolism at rank 3 (p = 2.52e-4) via mass-network proximity on the human_mfn graph, confirming the finding without annotation-dependent ID resolution. Galactose metabolism sits upstream of the Leloir pathway (GALM, GALK, GALT) and connects to glycerolipid metabolism through glycerol egress; the concurrent elevation of glycerol and myo-inositol is consistent with osmotic or membrane-stress perturbation reported in galactose-loaded cell models. react_result.final_narrative_text: Galactose metabolism is the dominant cross-paradigm signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052), MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG:hsa00052), and Mummichog m/z-direct (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) all converge on the same biological module with five shared driver metabolites: galactinol (C01235), sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactitol (C01697), and glycerol (C00116). RaMP reports a fold-enrichment of 1743x and FDR = 1.22e-15 for KEGG:map00052; MetaboAnalystR reports p = 9.53e-10 for KEGG:hsa00052 with 5 of 27 pathway compounds hit; Mummichog reports p = 5.04e-4 with 10 of 11 pathway compounds matched, indicating near-complete pathway activation. Galactinol is the alpha-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol conjugate that structurally bridges the galactose and inositol branches of this network. Glycerol additionally appears in the glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway (KEGG:hsa00561, p = 0.049) alongside myo-inositol, consistent with its dual role in sugar and membrane-lipid metabolism. Acetylcholine and 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 were not enriched in any ORA or m/z-direct result.
